Subject: Residency and temporary cross-region processing questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement I need two things clarified for our InfoSec / Data Protection team so we can progress the DPA:

- Can Redwood commit that inference and primary customer data for Helix Health will be pinned to the EU region (Frankfurt) by default? We expect strict residency for inference request payloads and derived embeddings.
- We understand operational realities (autoscaling, failover). Please confirm what transient cross-region processing you allow (analytics, telemetry, backups): maximum duration, triggers (maintenance vs outage), and whether any telemetry or logs ever leave the EU for processing / indexing.
- Please attach your current subprocessor roster and any ops runbook that describes failover steps and notification windows.

We need this evidence for our DPO to approve the DPA addendum. If you can share a sample DPA clause we can run internally.

Appreciate a short timeline — Carlos and I are trying to close this by end of month.

Best,
Ava Morgan
Head of Security Programs
Helix Health

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers up front, then we can share artifacts and schedule a short call:

- Short answer: yes — Redwood will pin primary inference and customer-level embeddings to an EU residency boundary for Helix Health under an addendum to the DPA.
- Transient processing: we allow timebound, telemetry/ops processing outside the EU only for specific operational reasons (e.g., autoscaling across an adjacent availability zone, short maintenance failovers). We classify these into: analytics (aggregation/metric computation) and backup-restores. We treat them differently: analytics windows are typically <= 4 hours and never include plaintext PII; backup restore windows (for disaster recovery) may require up to 72 hours outside-region in extreme DR scenarios but are subject to prior notification and customer approval where feasible.

I am attaching an ops playbook and our current subprocessor roster (see attachments). Marissa (Legal) is on copy and will propose precise DPA wording. Ben will follow on evidence for telemetry sanitization and KMS handling.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tuesday 14:00 CET to walk through the clauses and evidence. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign link for the DPA addendum.

Attachments: ops_runbook.pdf (ops playbook excerpt); subprocessor_roster.csv

Thanks,

Subject: Draft DPA addendum language — region pinning and transient processing

Ava / team,

Following Kimberly’s note, please find below (inline) the draft clause we recommend adding to the DPA to capture the commitments discussed. I’m including a short explanation of the operational guardrails. I’ll also attach a docx with the clause so your counsel can markup.

--- DRAFT CLAUSE (summary form) ---
1) Residency scope: Redwood will ensure that Customer data used for inference and embeddings for Helix Health is processed and stored within the EU (Frankfurt) while in active use.
2) Transient processing exceptions: Redwood may route or process Customer telemetry or operational artifacts outside the EU only for operational reasons (autoscaling, maintenance, incident mitigation). Such processing is limited to the minimum data necessary, is timebound, and will be logged.
   - Analytics/telemetry: max transient window 4 hours; data is aggregated/anonymized prior to any cross-region processing.
   - Backup/DR restores: in declared disaster-recovery scenarios, transient restoration may occur outside the EU for up to 72 hours unless otherwise agreed; Customer will be notified within 4 hours of the start of a restore event.
3) Subprocessors & controls: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessor roster and notify Customer of changes. All subprocessors will be contractually bound to the same residency commitments and security controls.
4) KMS & encryption: Customer-managed keys can be used for key material controlling backups and persistent storage.

Operational notes: logs and low-level telemetry used for service reliability are scrubbed of customer identifiers before cross-region aggregation. We do not export inference input payloads for analytics outside the EU.

I’ve attached the Word doc 'dpa_addendum_sample.docx' with the clause text and some redline-friendly notes. If Helix wants to propose edits we can accept tracked changes.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: dpa_addendum_sample.docx
